paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the God who ruins the proud is the same God who feeds the poor. Isaiah 25 opens with a song that says He has worked wonders, "plans formed long ago—in perfect faithfulness" (Isaiah 25:1). He has been "a refuge for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in distress" (Isaiah 25:4). So when the fortress falls into the dust (Isaiah 25:12), that is not a God who loses His temper. That's a God who keeps His word, and you can lean your whole weight on that.

Now look at the feast, because it's HUGE. "On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet for all the peoples" (Isaiah 25:6). Then comes the part that gets me every time: "He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face" (Isaiah 25:8). I bake cookies for a living, so I know a table is no small thing. But a table where death is gone and every tear is wiped? Friend, I'm running out of capital letters.

So here's why it matters to you today. Isaiah says the people in that day will say, "we have waited for Him, and He has saved us" (Isaiah 25:9). Waiting is not wasted time with this God. Keep your ovens ready, keep trusting what He has spoken, and let the promise of that day shape how you wait.
